summary: Iteration 3 retest against external REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. The HIGH bug from iteration_2 is FIXED. mjpeg_stream_async correctly triggers finally/remove_viewer on client disconnect. All 9 iteration_2 tests remain green AND 5 new targeted regression tests pass (14/14 total). Verified: (a) demo::0/1/4 fps drops to 0.0 within 6s after a 3s curl-style stream; (b) two concurrent viewers on demo::2 share the streamer (~15fps, not ~30) and drop to 0 after close; (c) Program Out with 3 tiles produces out_fps>15 and, on disable, all referenced sources drop to 0.0 within 6s — confirming no orphan streamers.
critical_code_review_comments: mjpeg_stream_async uses asyncio.run_in_executor for the blocking wait_next_frame + polls request.is_disconnected() between frames — clean and idiomatic.
Legacy sync mjpeg_stream() is kept for compat but no longer wired; consider deleting to avoid future confusion.
SourceStreamer.remove_viewer decrements _viewers; when it reaches 0 the capture loop exits and source.fps returns to 0 — verified end-to-end.
context_for_next_testing_agent: iteration_2 HIGH bug resolved. Base URL from /app/frontend/.env. Run pytest with -n 0 (tests share global streamer state). Two test files: test_multiview_perf.py (9 tests) and test_disconnect_cleanup.py (5 tests, targeted for the mjpeg_stream_async disconnect-cleanup fix).
rca of the issue: Fix confirmed: converting mjpeg_stream to async and polling request.is_disconnected() between frames while running the blocking wait_next_frame in an executor ensures Starlette can raise CancelledError into the async generator on disconnect, so the finally block reliably calls streamer.remove_viewer() and _viewers drops to 0.
